- Model consistently underestimates prices in the early part of the 30-day horizon, especially after sharp spikes or corrections.
- Overestimates in the middle-to-late period when prices are trending upward or recovering from lows.
- Shows significant lag in capturing recent price reversals; forecasts often miss sudden drops or spikes.
- Tends to overshoot after a price spike, then corrects too slowly — overcorrects in the following days.
- Mean reversion bias: model assumes prices will return to historical averages too quickly, ignoring structural or policy-driven deviations.
- Underestimates volatility in the final 5–7 days of the forecast horizon, especially when true outcomes show strong upward momentum.
- Overconfident in short-term momentum; fails to account for policy interventions or seasonal effects in the last 10 days.
- Often misjudges the timing of price peaks — forecasts peak too early or too late relative to actual market behavior.
